question: Can a recurrent public-history model jointly learn action-conditioned fault outcomes, CDL-style relevance and sparse CASM computation on coupled drifting maintenance tasks?

evidence_gate.inherited: DEV-054 null and reliability regression; existing SwiLAMTSK, LearnedCDL, structural workspace and ConditionalExecutor are substrates, not new evidence
evidence_gate.new_L2: Nonzero trained component gradients, incremental/batch parity, memory/routing/compute lesions
evidence_gate.new_L3: Paid closed-loop decisions with learned action outcomes under coupling and drift
evidence_gate.not_claimed: Original CDL teacher distillation, symbolic CASM-S program discovery, C5 scaling, real-world safety, commercial value, full architecture superiority

training.loss: BCE next joint fault marginals for the randomized executed action; supervised simulator-only post-action fault labels; runtime receives only public noisy sensors and paid inspection receipts
training.selection: Final checkpoint; no test-based recipe selection or plateau-as-convergence claim

world.coupling: repair can cause collateral fault on other entity; rate depends on hidden switching regime
world.drift: held-out continuous sinusoidal repair and collateral rates, outside the fitted two-regime HMM class
world.acquisition: Twelve randomized calibration actions on same physical world; all action expenses and intermediate residual-fault penalties included in total stream cost for every arm

hmm: Supervised training-only fit of 2x4-state action transition counts with Dirichlet .5 smoothing; latent regime hazard .1 fixed. Filter public sensors and exact paid inspection receipts; never read evaluation latent state. Independent baseline factorizes entity transitions and omits latent regime/coupling.
comparison: Same public history, observation channel, action candidates and one-step cost functional. GRU hidden size chosen by trainable parameter count within 2%; actual retained bytes and work reported, no padding parameters.
primary: Total physical stream cost including acquisition versus fitted_hmm (strong adaptive comparator); paired world-cluster bootstrap resampling model seeds globally, 2000 draws; simultaneous Bonferroni 95% intervals for four MTSK mechanism contrasts
reliability: No accepted improvement unless upper cost interval below zero versus matched GRU and fitted HMM, no increased total fault exposure for every seed/family, and feasible oracle headroom >=0.1/entity with positive lower paired 95% bound. Full-state one-step oracle is an information-privileged reference, not attainable Bayes-optimal performance.

stopping.this_batch: Complete all 15 fits, preserve crashes and negative results; no adaptive extension
stopping.retirement: At DEV-056, if a preregistered adequate-headroom benchmark does not establish MTSK superiority over matched GRU with reliability guard, retire the memory-novelty claim for this program; inadequate headroom is an inconclusive benchmark and does not authorize claiming novelty or indefinite postponement.

next_selective_computation: Separate DEV-057 contract for indexed acquisition, equal-bits scalar state and hash baselines. Do not infer C5 from fixed-size expert routing.
audit: Separate process restores every checkpoint, reproduces predictions, replays all recorded physical trajectories from deterministic seeds, verifies hashes. Same-author shared-code development audit only.
budget: 15 fixed-exposure CPU fits; 30 process-minute target. No paid remote compute. Smoke/test namespaces disjoint from registered splits. Native Veritas integration, if unavailable, must be reported unavailable rather than inferred from a local simulator.
autoresearch_reference: https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch/blob/master/program.md; adapted via research/autoresearch/program.md; fixed exposure and reliability gates supersede language-model val_bpb optimization
